paragraphs.title: A Plea for an Answer and Mercy in Distress

easy.explanation: He begins, “Hear my prayer, O LORD.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist pray to hear his prayer?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “For the enemy hath persecuted my soul.”
easy.q: Who has persecuted the psalmist’s soul?

easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “My heart within me is desolate.”
easy.q: What has happened to the psalmist’s heart?

answers: Because no living person can be justified in God’s sight
Because he does not know the LORD
Because he is not afraid of the enemy
medium.explanation: He acknowledges that “in thy sight shall no man living be justified.”
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD not to enter into judgment with him?

answers: It makes him sing with joy
It brings his life down and overwhelms his spirit
It causes him to forget the LORD
medium.explanation: The enemy has smitten his life down, and his spirit is overwhelmed.
medium.q: How does the enemy’s persecution affect the psalmist?

answers: A place of distress and desolation
medium.explanation: Dwelling in darkness pictures the psalmist’s severe distress.

answers: A plea for God’s answer amid a sense of distress and abandonment
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks God to answer while describing darkness, weakness, and trouble.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: He relies on his own strength
He expects help from his enemies
He depends on the LORD’s faithfulness and righteousness
challenge.explanation: He appeals to God’s character rather than claiming personal righteousness.
challenge.q: What does the request to be answered in God’s faithfulness and righteousness reveal about the psalmist’s hope?

answers: His life is brought down to the ground, while his spirit and heart are overwhelmed
He describes only fear of the future
challenge.explanation: The enemy strikes his life down, and his spirit and heart suffer within him.
challenge.q: How is the psalmist’s distress described both physically and inwardly?

paragraphs.title: Remembering the Past and Longing for God

easy.explanation: He says, “I remember the days of old.”

answers: The LORD’s works and the work of His hands
easy.explanation: He meditates on all God’s works and the work of His hands.
He says, “I stretch forth my hands unto thee.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist stretch forth his hands?

answers: It strengthens his longing for the LORD
It causes him to turn away from the LORD
It makes him forget his situation
medium.explanation: Remembering God’s works leads him to seek God in his trouble.
medium.q: How does remembering the past relate to the psalmist’s distress?

answers: The soul thirsts and needs the LORD
The soul is full of joy
medium.explanation: The image of thirsty land shows the intensity of his longing for God.
medium.q: What does comparing the soul to a thirsty land express?

answers: To remember what the LORD has done
To tell about weapons of war
medium.explanation: He reflects on God’s works and the work of His hands.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist mention the work of God’s hands?

answers: Remembering God’s works leads to prayer and longing for Him
Joy leads to giving up prayer
Anger leads to forgetting the past
challenge.explanation: The psalmist remembers God’s works, stretches out his hands, and thirsts for Him.
challenge.q: What emotional progression appears in these two verses?

answers: To emphasize the power of the enemy
To show the depth of the psalmist’s need and longing
challenge.explanation: The image vividly expresses his soul’s urgent desire for God.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the image of thirsty land?

answers: He expresses prayer, dependence, and longing
He declares that he needs no help
challenge.explanation: The gesture accompanies his appeal and shows dependence on the LORD.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from stretching forth his hands unto the LORD?

paragraphs.title: An Urgent Request for Guidance and the Right Path

easy.explanation: He asks, “Hear me speedily, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do quickly?

answers: The way in which he should walk
easy.explanation: He asks God to make him know “the way wherein I should walk.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask to know?

easy.explanation: He prays, “Deliver me, O LORD, from mine enemies.”
easy.q: From whom does the psalmist ask to be delivered?

answers: His spirit is failing, and he fears going down into the pit
He wants to hide from the enemy
He wants to forget the LORD
medium.explanation: He feels that his spirit is failing and asks not to be abandoned.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD not to hide His face?

answers: Because he trusts in the LORD, he asks to know the way he should walk
Because he does not trust, he refuses to move
Because he has won, he needs no guidance
medium.explanation: His trust in God leads him to seek God’s lovingkindness and direction.
medium.q: How are trust and guidance connected in verse 8?

medium.explanation: He asks the LORD’s good Spirit to lead him in a morally upright way.
medium.q: What does “the land of uprightness” represent in context?

answers: A speedy answer, mercy, guidance, deliverance, and instruction in God’s will
challenge.explanation: The psalmist moves from urgent help to guidance, rescue, and obedience.
challenge.q: What sequence of requests appears in verses 7–10?

answers: He places his hope in the LORD and therefore seeks guidance and deliverance
He announces that he is turning away from the LORD
He is addressing only his enemies
challenge.explanation: Lifting up his soul expresses trust and dependence on God.
challenge.q: How does “I lift up my soul unto thee” relate to the requests that follow?

challenge.explanation: He prays, “Teach me to do thy will.”
challenge.q: What does the psalmist ask to learn besides being rescued from danger?

paragraphs.title: Life, Deliverance, and Victory over the Troublers of the Soul

easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do for him?

easy.explanation: He asks God to bring his soul “out of trouble.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to bring his soul out of?

easy.explanation: He concludes, “For I am thy servant.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe himself at the end?

answers: For the sake of his wealth
medium.explanation: He says, “Quicken me, O LORD, for thy name’s sake.”
medium.q: For whose sake does the psalmist ask the LORD to quicken him?

answers: Cut them off and destroy them
medium.explanation: He asks God to cut off his enemies and destroy those who afflict him.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do to his enemies and those who afflict his soul?

answers: It expresses his belonging to the LORD and his appeal for protection
It proves that he is God’s enemy
medium.explanation: Calling himself God’s servant emphasizes his relationship with and dependence on the LORD.
medium.q: How does identifying himself as God’s servant relate to his request?

answers: His own power and his enemies’ help
challenge.explanation: He asks to be quickened for God’s name’s sake and rescued for God’s righteousness’ sake.
challenge.q: On what two grounds does the psalmist ask for life and deliverance?

answers: He asks for deliverance and declares that he is God’s servant
He abandons all relationship with the LORD
He asks only for personal victory without reference to God
challenge.explanation: His requests for help end with the statement, “For I am thy servant.”
challenge.q: How does the ending combine a personal plea with faithfulness to the LORD?

answers: The psalm moves from asking for guidance to asking for life, deliverance, and victory over enemies
It moves from remembrance to complete forgetfulness
It moves from prayer to celebration
challenge.explanation: After seeking direction and obedience, the psalmist asks for life, rescue, and judgment on his enemies.
challenge.q: What conceptual movement occurs from the preceding verses to the final verses?
